title: Push-forward of compactly supported integer multiplicity currents by a map that is C¹ near the support (Simon 6.2.23–2.29, 3.3–3.9)
statement:
Let P, m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, O ⊆ ℝ^P open, and f : ℝ^P → ℝ^P C¹ on O (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f O). Then there is a map push : 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) → 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with the following properties.
(A) Let Y ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) be integer multiplicity with spt Y compact and spt Y ⊆ O, and let (M, θ, ξ) be any integer multiplicity representation of Y. Then:
 (i) push Y(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·⟨ω(f(x)) ∘ ΛⁿDf(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P). Here (ω(f(x)) ∘ ΛⁿDf(x))(v₁, …, vₙ) = ω(f(x))(Df(x)v₁, …, Df(x)vₙ); in Lean, (ω (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x).
 (ii) push Y is integer multiplicity.
 (iii) spt push Y ⊆ f(spt Y).
 (iv) For every real L with ‖Df(y)‖ ≤ L for all y ∈ O, M(push Y) ≤ Lⁿ·M(Y), as ENNReal.ofReal (L^n) * M(Y).
 (v) If ∂Y = 0, then ∂(push Y) = 0.
(B) push(Y₁ − Y₂) = push Y₁ − push Y₂ for all integer multiplicity Y₁, Y₂ ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with compact supports contained in O.
This is f_#Y of Simon 2.24(2) and 3.9.
lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (O : Set (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → Euclid P), IsOpen O → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f O → ∃ push : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1) → GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1), (∀ (Y : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)), R.Represents Y → IsCompact Y.support → Y.support ⊆ O → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1), push Y ω = ∫ x in R.carrier, (R.mult x : ℝ) * R.orient x (((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (m + 1)) (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)) ∂μHE[m + 1]) ∧ IsIntegerMultiplicity (push Y) ∧ (push Y).support ⊆ f '' Y.support ∧ (∀ L : ℝ, (∀ y ∈ O, ‖fderiv ℝ f y‖ ≤ L) → (push Y).mass ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (L ^ (m + 1)) * Y.mass) ∧ (Y.boundary = 0 → (push Y).boundary = 0)) ∧ ∀ Y₁ Y₂ : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1), IsIntegerMultiplicity Y₁ → IsIntegerMultiplicity Y₂ → IsCompact Y₁.support → Y₁.support ⊆ O → IsCompact Y₂.support → Y₂.support ⊆ O → push (Y₁ - Y₂) = push Y₁ - push Y₂
